description: Comprehension test set for CVE-2026-42945. Each question is a yes/no claim with a ground truth checked against the nginx source (release-1.30.0 and release-1.30.1) and, where marked, against measured lab findings (F-n) from the author's M.Tech security assessment of this CVE. Questions marked knownError are claims an LLM assistant got wrong during that assessment (its corrections log). Questions sharing a pair id ask the same thing of the vulnerable and the patched code base; a model that reads the code should get both right, one that guesses tends to give the same answer twice.

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.0, does ngx_http_script_regex_end_code reset e->is_args to 0 before it returns?
questions.evidence: 1.30.0 ngx_http_script_regex_end_code resets e->quote but not e->is_args. Adding `e->is_args = 0;` there is the entire 1.30.1 fix (upstream commit 524977e).

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.1, does ngx_http_script_regex_end_code reset e->is_args to 0 before it returns?
In nginx 1.30.1, was CVE-2026-42945 fixed by adding a bounds check to ngx_http_script_copy_capture_code?
questions.evidence: ngx_http_script_copy_capture_code is unchanged between 1.30.0 and 1.30.1; the fix resets is_args in ngx_http_script_regex_end_code so the two passes agree. Tests whether the model reads the code or assumes the usual shape of an overflow patch.

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.0, when ngx_http_script_complex_value_code computes the length of a value such as the one in set $x "$1", does that length pass see the is_args flag of the main script engine?
questions.evidence: The length pass runs on a local engine `le` cleared with ngx_memzero; only le.quote is copied from e, so le.is_args is 0 and captures are counted unescaped.

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.0, can ngx_http_script_copy_capture_code write a regex capture URI-escaped, so that one input byte becomes three output bytes, when e->is_args is set and the request URI contained a '+' or a percent-encoded character?
questions.evidence: If (e->is_args || e->quote) && (quoted_uri || plus_in_uri), the capture is written with ngx_escape_uri(..., NGX_ESCAPE_ARGS), turning '+' into %2B.

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.0, if a captured value contains n '+' characters and is copied by a set directive after a rewrite whose replacement contains '?', does the copy write 2n more bytes than the buffer allocated for it?
questions.evidence: Each '+' is counted as 1 byte in the length pass and written as 3 (%2B) in the copy pass, 2 extra bytes each. Measured in the lab as an overrun of exactly 2n bytes: buffer sized n+5, filled with 3n+5 (F-3).

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.0, for a later set $x "$1" to overflow, must the preceding rewrite's replacement string itself reference a capture such as $1? Answer YES if a capture in the replacement is required, NO if a '?' in the replacement is enough.
questions.evidence: ngx_http_script_compile adds the args code (ngx_http_script_start_args_code, which sets e->is_args = 1) when it meets '?' in the replacement, whether or not the replacement has variables. Lab: only the '?' is required (F-6). The LLM assistant had claimed a capture was also needed.

questions.query: In nginx 1.30.0, if the rewrite whose replacement contains '?' carries the break flag, can a set $x "$1" that follows it in the same location still overflow?
questions.evidence: break stops the rewrite module's script for that location, so the following set never runs. Lab: two configs differing only in break gave five sanitizer reports and zero (F-9). The LLM assistant had treated any '?' rewrite as sufficient.

questions.query: If an affected nginx 1.30.0 server returns HTTP 200 for a request whose URI contains a long run of '+' characters, does that show the heap buffer was not overrun?
questions.evidence: The overrun happens at every length; whether it crashes depends on what lies after the buffer. Lab: on an uninstrumented build an 800-character path overran by 1,600 bytes and still returned HTTP 200 with nothing logged (F-4). This is a reasoning question; the answer is not stated in any single function.
